summary: The configuration-contract step has compatibility defects that can silently change the selected reviewer or processing provider.

outcomes.evidence: Focused reproductions found three settings precedence and legacy migration defects. The existing six slot-settings tests pass but do not cover these cases.

checks: Passed: timeout 60s env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=<scratch> python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_slot_settings.py (6 tests).
Ran a bounded Python reproduction of initial_settings and apply_overrides: a Claude reviewer request with an explicit Codex processing default resolves processing to Claude.
Ran a bounded Python reproduction of legacy-manifest loading with canonical defaults: a saved Claude configuration resolves to the default Codex slot and processing configuration.
Ran a bounded Python reproduction of a legacy manifest containing only reviewers=['codex']: processing resolves to Claude. The baseline validator selected the sole reviewer.
blocking: In lib/pr_review/settings.py:114, apply_overrides forces the sole requested reviewer as processing provider even when defaults explicitly select another provider. This defeats the explicit processing selection honored by initial_settings.

In lib/pr_review/settings.py:150, loading a legacy manifest merges provider-based settings into initial canonical defaults without removing reviewer_slots or processing. Those defaults then take precedence over the saved configuration, silently changing the resumed session.

In lib/pr_review/settings.py:23 and lib/pr_review/settings.py:70, historical defaults insert processing_provider before normalization. A legacy single-Codex configuration that omitted this field therefore selects Claude, whereas the baseline validator selected Codex.
